content.text:
Let me analyze this carefully.

The ticket: Karen Black (E008) requests admin access to Source Code.

Most agents (HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities) say: role Payroll Specialist, employment type full_time. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role. For full-time employees, up to write; admin only if role owns the system. Payroll Specialist doesn't own Source Code (Engineer does). So max is write. Requested admin > write, so grant write.

Security agent says: employment type contractor, basic security training, recommendation read. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. So max is read. Grant read.

There's a conflict: most say full-time, security says contractor. How to decide? As the Approver, I need to weigh the evidence. Five agents agree on full-time Payroll Specialist; one (Security) claims contractor. The security agent's DB shows contractor. Hmm.

Which source should be trusted? Typically HR is the authority on employment type. HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities all say full-time. Security says contractor. The majority evidence supports full-time Payroll Specialist.

The employee is Karen Black. Other notes from ticket 1... all about E008. Only security disagrees.

Given the preponderance of evidence, I'll go with full-time Payroll Specialist. Max for full-time Payroll Specialist on Source Code is write (since admin requires owning role = Engineer). Requested admin exceeds write, so grant write.

Actually, let me think about whether the security note should override. The security agent's note says "Security DB shows employee E008 is a contractor" - it differs from others. This is a factual conflict. As Approver, I have to decide. Five notes say full-time, one says contractor. HR is typically the authoritative source for employment type. I'll trust the majority and HR.

Decision: grant write (maximum for full-time non-owner, since requested admin > write).

Let me submit with reasoning.
